summary: The article provides a largely accurate and well-structured explanation of the RBI repo rate hike and its impact on home loans, with most factual claims verified against authoritative sources.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has increased the repo rate by 25 basis points (bps) to 5.50% on October 7, 2026.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the RBI MPC meeting on October 7, 2026, and the 25 bps hike to 5.50%.

claims.claim: Since October 2019, most new floating rate retail loans, including home loans, have been mandated to be linked to an external benchmark.
claims.note: RBI's external benchmark framework became applicable to specified new floating-rate loans from October 1, 2019.

claims.claim: The reset frequency for EBLR-linked loans is usually at least once every three months, meaning the impact of the hike will be felt within this period.
claims.note: External benchmark-linked rates are required to be reset at least once every three months under the applicable RBI framework.

claims.claim: MCLR rates are usually reset after a period of 6 months or 1 year, depending on the loan agreement.
claims.note: MCLR-linked loans generally follow a reset cycle mentioned in the loan agreement. Depending on the loan type, the reset frequency may be monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or yearly.

claims.claim: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meets at least six times a year, typically every two months, to review the economic situation and decide on policy rates, including the repo rate.
claims.note: The MPC usually meets once every two months, i.e., 6 times a year.

claims.claim: Under Section 24(b) of the Income Tax Act, you can claim a deduction of up to ₹2 lakhs on the interest paid on a home loan for a self-occupied property. For rented properties, the entire interest paid can be deducted.
claims.note: Section 24(b) allows a deduction of up to ₹2 lakh for self-occupied properties. For rented properties, the entire interest paid can be claimed, though the maximum loss from house property that can be set off against other income is limited to ₹2 lakh.

article_title: RBI Repo Rate Hike: Impact on Your Home Loan EMI
